title: Heat Advisory
location: Lower Treasure Valley; Upper Treasure Valley; Oregon Lower Treasure Valley

details.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 101 expected.

* WHERE...Treasure Valley Zones.

* WHEN...From 2 PM MDT /1 PM PDT/ this afternoon to 9 PM MDT /8 PM
PDT/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses, especially
for the young, elderly, and animals.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Cochise, AZ

details.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 230 AM MST.

* At 1140 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the Douglas area. Between
0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up
to 0.25 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Douglas, Bisbee-Douglas Airport and Pirtleville.

This includes the following highways...
Route 80 between mile markers 355 and 388. Route 191 between mile
markers 1 and 9.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Black Draw, Silver Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Mulberry Canyon,
Whitewater Draw and Danger Wash.
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

details.instruction:
A Heat Advisory is issued when the combination of heat and humidity
is expected to make it feel like it is 95 to 99 degrees for two or
more consecutive days, or 100 to 104 degrees for any length of time.

Seniors and those with chronic health problems or mental health
conditions are at an increased risk. Homes without air conditioning
can be much hotter than outdoor temperatures.

Use air conditioning to stay cool at home or go to a place that has
air conditioning. If you don't have home air conditioning, continue
to seek out cool spaces each day as long as it remains hot, and for
a few days after if your home is still hot. Check on vulnerable
friends, family members and neighbors.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! In cases of heat stroke call 9 1 1.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of

interiors can reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.
